svg.text: Every screen speaks to one REST API over HTTPS. None of them hold keys or reach the chain.
The diner experience on a laptop. Shows the
live curve for one night and handles buying a
table, selling it back, and holdings.
The same diner flows rebuilt for a phone, as
bottom sheets and a scrolling night rail.
Where a venue opens a pool per party size,
watches fill and reserve, checks diners in at
the door, and sweeps after service.
An offline explorer for the pricing model.
Scrubbing the time until service redraws the
Owns the API, identity and money. Reaches the chain only through chain-services.
The only endpoint a client calls. Serves pool
listings and quotes, and accepts buy, sell,
Runs a trade end to end: locks a quote,
Rejects and refunds if the price moved first.
One middleware resolves the app user id on
every call. Stubbed today, a JWT provider
later; an issuer role gates the venue routes.
Collects payment against a locked quote and
pays sell-backs out by transfer. A stub
implementation runs the demo without keys.
The only module that imports a chain client. The mock shipped first, so no other stream waited on devnet.
quote, buy, sell, redeem, check_in and sweep.
An in-memory chain enforcing the same pricing
and trading rules as the program, so the whole
Signs and sends program instructions, reads
the pool and reserve accounts, and subscribes
Writes program events into Postgres so the UI
reads prices, history and holdings from a
database rather than an RPC node.
The single source of truth for funds. Everything above it is derived state.
Per-pool state: the curve parameters, tables
sold and available, the venue cut, and the
Holds the USDC for one pool. Its balance is
the area under the curve up to the tables
sold, and the venue sweeps it after service.
Opening a pool, buying, selling back,
redeeming at the door, check-in, and the
sweep. A buy mints one fungible token.
The program derives θ from block time on each
trade, so decay can never be supplied by a
caller. Trading stops at service time.
in-process calls, never the chain directly
One pool is one venue, one service window, one party size.
Each table sold raises the price of the next. The curve is
always the counterparty, so a table can always be sold back.
τ is the time left before service. The premium fades linearly
across the final Tc, and the meal credit p₀ never decays.
φ is the venue cut, kept on every resale. It is the spread
between what a buyer pays and what a seller receives.
Every buy adds p(n) and every sell-back removes p(n−1), so the
reserve always covers a sell-back. Decay only leaves surplus.
Frozen interfaces and the pricing functions, imported by every
layer. The chain and the model run the same code.
The bonding curve is the smart contract. Postgres is a read cache and is never authoritative over money.
